title: Add with wraparound, no UB
hints: Unsigned arithmetic in C is defined to wrap modulo 2^32. Signed is not.
Convert both inputs to `uint32_t`, add them there, then convert the sum back to `int32_t`.
The add itself must happen on the unsigned values: cast before the `+`, not after.

answer.explain: `(uint32_t)a + (uint32_t)b` wraps by definition, so there is no undefined behavior. Converting that out-of-range 32-bit pattern back to `int32_t` is implementation-defined in C, and every compiler you'll use (GCC, Clang, MSVC) reads it as two's complement, so `INT_MAX + 1` comes out as `INT_MIN`.
